Hi Emily / Carlos,

Thanks again for taking time today — really helpful conversation. Quick recap + proposed next steps from our side related to logging and PII concerns: 

Summary of ask from FintechCo:
- No storage of unredacted PII in request/response logs (PII = SSNs, card numbers, unmasked account IDs)
- Ability to redact or hash identifiers and headers (authorization tokens, internal trace IDs)
- Configurable retention windows for request logs (minimum 30 days, preferred 90 days)
- Option for EU-only data residency for logs originating from EU customers
- Audit evidence for redaction effectiveness for SOC 2 review

Redwood options we propose (high level):
1) Real-time PII detection + automatic redaction: configurable regex + ML-based detectors to mask SSNs, PANs, emails, etc.
2) Header and trace ID scrubbing: default scrub list for common headers (Authorization, Cookie, X-Trace-ID) with ability to add custom header names.
3) Sampling & storage controls: full request logging off by default, or sampled at 0.1% for debugging; customers can opt into full logging for specific routes with explicit consent.
4) Retention & export: configurable retention windows (30/90/365 days) and one-click export for audit.
5) Data residency: logs can be pinned to region-specific storage (US / EU) depending on account settings.

Attached: redwood-logging-controls.pdf — technical explainer + config examples.

Thanks for the context — this is straightforward but a few implementation notes and trade-offs to call out: 

Recommended approach (best balance of security + debuggability):
- ML+regex layered redaction for request/response bodies: use strict regex for high-confidence patterns (PAN, SSN) and ML detectors for names/emails to reduce false negatives. Replace detected fields with tokenized placeholders (e.g., <REDACTED:SSN> or <HASH:acct_XXXXX>).
- Hash vs strip for trace IDs: hashing (HMAC-SHA256 with customer-managed key) preserves correlation while preventing exposure. Note: hashed values will still allow correlation across services only if the same hashing key and normalization are used.
- Headers: default deny-list (Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie, Proxy-Authorization). Allow customer to add extra header names via admin UI or API.
- Sampling: keep full request bodies disabled by default. For routes where customers request full logs for short-term debugging, allow time-limited opt-in (e.g., 24–72 hours) with elevated audit logging of who accessed.
- Retention: implement configurable retention buckets (30/90/365) as policy labels. Ensure backups and exports respect the selected bucket.

Known limitations / items for product to verify:
- We need to ensure our structured redaction engine includes language-agnostic name detection for non-English names (FintechCo has APAC customers).
- Redaction verification report: we can provide sampling-based coverage metrics and example hashed values (not reversible without key). For SOC 2, we should include: rule-set inventory, sample before/after, and access logs for redaction configuration changes.

Attachments: redwood-redaction-config.yaml (example config snippets for their lists and regex).

Suggested next steps:
1) We build a proposed redaction config and send to Emily for review (includes rule-set and sample before/after).
2) Offer a 30-min tech deep-dive with our security engineer (propose Tue Dec 7, 10:00 PST).
